in_hebrew.name: שילומיאה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שילומיאה הוא שם שמשמעותו 'אלוהים הוא השלום שלי' או 'השלום של אלוהים'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'שלום' (שלום) ו-'אלוהים' (אלוהים). השם נגזר מהשורש 'ש-ל-מ' שפירושו 'שלום' או 'שלמות'. השם שילומיאה משמש כהבעת תפילה לאלוהים שיביא שלום ושלווה לחייהם של הילדים.

in_greek.name: Σιλωμια
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σιλωμια προέρχεται από τις εβραϊκές λέξεις 'שלום' (Shalom) και 'אלוהים' (Elohim), που σημαίνει 'ο Θεός είναι η ειρήνη μου' ή 'η ειρήνη του Θεού'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, η έννοια της ειρήνης συνδέεται στενά με την παρουσία και τη σχέση με τον Θεό. Το όνομα αυτό αντανακλά την πνευματική σημασία της ειρήνης και της αρμονίας με τον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Shilomea
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Shilomea derivatur ex verbis hebraicis 'שלום' (Shalom) et 'אלוהים' (Elohim), quae significant 'Deus meus pax est' vel 'Pax Dei'. Nomen hoc pietatem et pacem cum Deo exprimit. In traditione christiana, nomen Shilomea significat fiduciam in Deum ut fontem pacis et salutis.

in_english.name: Shilomea
in_english.meaning: God is my peace or complete peace
in_english.long_meaning: The name Shilomea originates from Hebrew roots 'שלום' (Shalom) meaning 'peace' and 'אלוהים' (Elohim) meaning 'God'. It signifies 'God is my peace' or 'complete peace'. The name conveys a deep spiritual meaning, expressing trust in God as the source of peace and wholeness. Historically, names with similar roots are found in biblical contexts, emphasizing the importance of divine peace in one's life. Today, Shilomea is used across Christian cultures to symbolize a prayer for peace and divine presence.

In Jewish tradition, the name Shalom is used as a greeting, expressing a desire for peace and goodwill towards others. This peaceful sentiment can be fostered through acts of kindness, community building, and spiritual practices.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Shilomea represents a deep sense of peace and tranquility. It serves as a reminder that no matter what is happening in our lives, we can find peace and comfort in God. The name encourages us to cultivate a deep and abiding faith, trusting that God is with us every step of the way.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The Syriac Chronicle of 724 AD mentions a bishop named Shalema (Shilomea) of Damascus. The name Shilomea carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Syriac Chronicle is a historical work written in Syriac language which covers events from the creation of the world until the year 724 AD.

historical_references.reference: The Greek historian Theophanes mentions a bishop named Shilomea who was the patriarch of Antioch in the late 5th or early 6th century AD.
historical_references.context: Theophanes the Confessor was a Byzantine historian who wrote a historical work known as the 'Chronicle'. He covered the period from the creation of the world until the year 813 AD.
